item: the key-file wrap removes keys/.pending only under the lock, checks its copy outside it, and a creation flushes the removal of its private name (hardening review rows 6 to 8 on #1932)
summary: BEFORE: replace_in_place's last step (drop_pending) ran outside KEY_FILES_LOCK and could remove keys/.pending between another wrap's rename out of it and that wrap's flush of it, so the flush failed and the replaced plaintext key's bytes were never overwritten (row 6); the check of the wrapped copy, a second key derivation, ran inside the lock, so an emergency erase waited one derivation per wrap in flight (row 7); create_new removed its private name, a second name for the key's bytes, without flushing that removal, so a power cut could bring a plaintext alias back until the next wrap (row 8). NOW: drop_pending runs under the lock; check runs on the sealed bytes before the lock and the private copy is compared with them byte for byte under it (a copy that does not read back is never used); create_new flushes keys/.pending after removing its private name. 5 tests, 4 red on main. Release line: none (internal hardening of the key-file wrap; no visible change).
